name: Julius Nyerere International Airport
before:
Tanzania's main international airport, in the Kipawa ward of Dar es Salaam, with flights across Africa and out to Asia, Europe and the Middle East.

There are three terminals and it pays to know which one. Terminal 3, opened in August 2019, handles all international flights and holds 58 shops and services. Terminal 2 takes domestic and regional scheduled flights and is rated for 1.5 million passengers. Terminal 1 is for private, charter and small aircraft, and a separate VIP terminal for state and high profile passengers was built in January 2026.

Terminal 2 is due a major rebuild, announced in 2024, to turn it into a national hub for Air Tanzania handling up to 3.5 million passengers, so expect the domestic side to change.

A rail shuttle from the airport into the city has been proposed and coaches were bought, but check whether it is running before relying on it.

The airport was renamed after Julius Nyerere, Tanzania's first president, in stages between 2005 and 2006.
after:
The international airport for Dar es Salaam, Tanzania's largest city, with flights across Africa and out to Asia, Europe and the Middle East.

There are three terminals, so check which one a client's flight uses. Terminal 3, the newest, opened in 2019. A new VIP terminal for state guests opened at Terminal 1 in January 2026. Terminal 2 is due to be modernised and expanded, so expect changes there.

It is named after Julius Nyerere, Tanzania's first president.

claims.note: The ministry's table of international airlines at JNIA (May 2026) has Amsterdam and Istanbul (Europe), Dubai, Doha and Muscat (Middle East), Mumbai and Guangzhou on Air Tanzania (Asia) and a long list of African routes. Middle East flights were suspended from 28 February 2026 in the Iran war; the ministry's May table and Emirates' own live page show them running again.

claims.note: The 2024 plan (TAA and Wikipedia) was a rebuild as a national hub for Air Tanzania for up to 3.5 million passengers. The 2026/27 budget funds 'Modernization and Expansion of Julius Nyerere International Airport Terminal Building II' (TZS 26.75 billion) but gives neither the hub role nor a capacity, so those details are dropped. ch-aviation (18 May 2026) reported a new 2.5 million passenger terminal 'at Dar es Salaam' from the same budget, but the speech puts that terminal at Mwanza, so ch-aviation is not used.

claims.claim: Terminal 3 opened August 2019, all international flights, 58 shops and services
claims.wasBefore: Terminal 3, opened in August 2019, handles all international flights and holds 58 shops and services.
claims.why: The 2019 opening is kept. No source from the last 12 months says Terminal 3 takes all international flights (the operator said so in October 2024), so the allocation is not stated. The 58 businesses rest on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: Terminal 2 domestic and regional, 1.5 million capacity
claims.wasBefore: Terminal 2 takes domestic and regional scheduled flights and is rated for 1.5 million passengers.
claims.why: Allocation not confirmed by any source from the last 12 months, and the terminal is due to be modernised and expanded; the old capacity figure is dropped with it.

claims.claim: Terminal 1 private, charter and small aircraft; VIP terminal built January 2026
claims.wasBefore: Terminal 1 is for private, charter and small aircraft, and a separate VIP terminal for state and high profile passengers was built in January 2026.
claims.why: Terminal 1's use for private, charter and small aircraft rests on Wikipedia alone. The VIP terminal is kept, corrected: it opened (was inaugurated) on 16 January 2026, at Terminal 1.

claims.claim: Terminal 2 rebuild announced 2024 as Air Tanzania hub for 3.5 million; domestic side to change
claims.wasBefore: Terminal 2 is due a major rebuild, announced in 2024, to turn it into a national hub for Air Tanzania handling up to 3.5 million passengers, so expect the domestic side to change.
claims.why: The works are kept with the 2026/27 budget. The hub role and 3.5 million figure come from 2024 and are not repeated in any source from the last 12 months; 'the domestic side' assumes an allocation that is not confirmed.

claims.wasBefore: A rail shuttle from the airport into the city has been proposed and coaches were bought, but check whether it is running before relying on it.
claims.why: A 2014 position from Wikipedia. Nothing current confirms a rail shuttle; the airports authority and the railway signed a general agreement on linking air and rail in September 2025, which names no airport service.

claims.wasBefore: The airport was renamed after Julius Nyerere, Tanzania's first president, in stages between 2005 and 2006.
claims.why: The namesake is kept with the operator. The 2005 and 2006 dates rest on Wikipedia alone: the Guardian (IPP Media) reports it cites could not be fetched (security check; archive copies blocked).
